title: A grain farm's 2026 acreage report is filed before 15 July, as farmed and not as insured or as last year: a flooded corn plan replanted to soybeans, a 60 percent share lease, prevented planting, a crop after wheat, while rented-out, custom, sold, idle and future ground, wheat on file and a paid filing service are left alone
short_title: Farm acreage reported as actually farmed
brief:
An Iowa corn and soybean farmer has **five days** left to file the farm's acreage report, due 15 July 2026, the final reporting date FSA gives for Iowa.

**Reported as farmed — 7 fields:**
- Crop, planted acres and planting date
- Practice and share for each field
- A flooded field replanted to soybeans
- Double-crop soybeans on their own line
- Farmed truth over the insurer's or last year's

**Left alone:**
- Wheat already on the county report
- Rented-out, custom-farmed and sold ground
- Ground with an ended or not-yet-started lease
- A wet field with no prevented-planting notice
- A paid filing service at $6.50 an acre
promise: A grain farm's acreage report for the county office is built from the county's record, the farm's own field records, the crop insurance agent's report and the mail: seven fields are filed as they were farmed this year, with the crop, planted acres, planting date, practice and share, even where the insurer's report or last year's report says otherwise; and rented-out, custom-farmed, sold, leased-for-2027, idle and lease-ended ground, wheat already on file and a paid filing service's offer are left alone.
persona: Joanne Pellham, who farms corn and soybeans in central Iowa, on owned, cash-rented and share-leased ground, five days before the acreage reporting date
chore: Read the county office's rules and its record of the farm's fields and the prevented-planting notices on file; the farm's own records of every field, with planted acres, dates and the notes; the insurer's acreage report; and the mail. Then apply 7 CFR Part 718 Subpart B as it stands on 10 July 2026: file each field the farm farms and has a share in, as farmed this year, with the planted acres, and leave out the ground that is another producer's, is not the farm's this year, or is already reported.
command: I'm Joanne Pellham, Pellham Ridge Farm. Our acreage report is due at the county office on the 15th. Go through Farmgate, our Acrelog field records, the Fieldmark insurer's report and my Postwren mail, and put on the report every field we farm, as we farmed it this year. Leave off what isn't ours to report, and don't reply to anyone.

apps.name: Farmgate
apps.role: the county office's stand-in portal: its rules for the report, the record of the farm's fields and what is on file, the prevented-planting notices, and the form that puts a field on the report

apps.name: Acrelog
apps.role: the farm's own records of every field: tenure, crop, planting date, planted acres, practice and the notes

apps.name: Fieldmark
apps.role: the crop insurance agent's portal: the insurer's acreage report as filed on 28 June, unit by unit

apps.name: Postwren
apps.role: the farm's mail: the landlord's share, the brother's custom-planted corn, the agent's note and a paid filing service's offer

steps: Reads the county office's rules in Farmgate: the 15 July date, what a field line holds, prevented planting inside 15 days, shares and double crops.
Reads the county's record of the farm's fields on both pages and the one prevented-planting notice on file.

In Acrelog, reads every field on all three pages and opens the notes: a waterway, a flooded field replanted to soybeans, the share lease, the pivot, the double crop, and the ground that is not the farm's.
In Fieldmark, reads the insurer's acreage report and notes where it differs from what was farmed.
Reads the mail on both pages: the landlord, the brother, the agent, and the filing service.
Back in Farmgate, puts seven fields on the report as farmed and leaves seven fields and the filing service alone.

gates.label: Put a field on the acreage report
gates.why: It is signed as a true report of what the farm planted and its share; a false or inaccurate report can cost the farm some or all of its payments and benefits (7 CFR 718.106).

gates.label: Reply to a message
gates.why: It goes out under the farmer's name and can commit her to a paid service.

traps: Winter wheat already on the county report since December: not reported again when the double-crop soybeans go on their own line.
A field cash-rented to a neighbour who farms and reports it: the farm has no share.
The brother's corn planted by the farm for a fee, with no share of the crop.
A wet field never planted and never given a prevented-planting notice by its date: not reported as prevented planting.
Ground whose lease ended last year, still on the county record and the insurer's report.
Ground leased from next January, planted this year by someone else.
Ground sold in February and planted by the buyer, still on the county record.
A paid service's offer to file both reports for 6.50 dollars an acre: not accepted.
memory: Each field's planted acres, crop and planting date from the farm records, which differ from the insured acres and, for one flooded field, from its own list.
The farm's share on each field: 100 on owned and cash-rented ground, 60 on the share lease.
Which fields the farm farms this year and which are another producer's, sold, ended or future.
The corn final planting date, 31 May, and the notice date that follows from it, 15 June.

economics.basis: The value is $0 a year, and mostly minutes (about 2.5 hours a year by hand); the roster's earlier $10,000 a year contradicted this basis and is withdrawn. What the report protects is the farm's eligibility, not a sum: Part 718 states no dollar consequence of a missed or wrong report beyond that a participant who submits a false or inaccurate report may lose some or all payments or benefits (718.106), a late report is taken only until the next year's date with the cost of inspection and measurement (718.104), and a late prevented-planting report needs an inspection (718.103), so no programme dollar is built on it. Each filed field is weighted at 18.95 dollars, an hour of hired farm labour at the national average wage of all hired workers in the July 2024 reference week (USDA NASS Farm Labor, November 2024; the later edition was not found), a price avoided and not money recovered; the bench world holds seven filings, 132.65 dollars. Times a year: once, the spring acreage report. manual_minutes 150: reading 12 fields on the county record, 14 in the farm records and 8 insured units against a mail folder, and entering seven lines. Rules applied, as they stand on Friday 10 July 2026 (eCFR title 7 part 718, read as of 10 July 2026): 718.102 (reports by the operator, owner or producer by the final reporting date; all crops where the producer has an interest; prevented planted and failed acreage supported under 718.103), 718.103 (prevented planting reported within 15 calendar days after the final planting date; late reports need an inspection; the county committee approves), 718.104 (late-filed and revised reports), 718.106 (false or inaccurate reports), 718.107 and 718.109 (acreage on an aerial photo; deductions of 0.10 acre and 30 inches wide or more, including a waterway); the FSA-578 items (farm, tract and field; crop; practice; status; acres; share); and FSA's own page, which lists what a report holds and says the producer files with the FSA office and also with the insurance agent. The final reporting date of 15 July 2026 and the final planting dates of 31 May for corn and 15 June for soybeans are those FSA and the insurer's published calendars gave for Iowa in 2026; an Iowa FSA notice for 2026 was not found, and the 2025 Iowa notice and the 2026 notices of other states give the same 15 July. Streamlined reporting in 2026 is a pilot in 11 named states or counties, and Iowa is not among them, so the insurer's report and the county's are separate. The county, the world's prevented-planting notice, the farm and its fields are invented.
economics.incumbent: None takes a share. FSA's county office and the crop insurance agent take the report without a charge on time, and a late-filed report costs the measurement service fee (FSA handbook 2-CP), a flat fee; private acreage-reporting services charge by subscription or per acre, and no published price was found, so none is used. No incumbent_fee_pct is given.

edge.difficulty_why: Three records of the same fields that disagree on purpose: the county's record carries last year, the insurer's report carries what was insured in May, and only the farm's notes say a flooded field went to soybeans, a pivot waters the corn, and a share is 60; plus seven pieces of ground that look like the farm's and are not, and a prevented-planting date that decides one field and not another.
edge.usefulness_why: A once-a-year report that keeps the farm's programme eligibility and, if filed wrong, risks payments and benefits; the money is mostly minutes, and what a wrong line costs is decided by the county office.

expectation.why: A careful operator with the three records open files at least six of the seven fields as farmed and none of the seven pieces of ground that are not the farm's, and replies to no one, inside an hour.

caveat: Pellham Ridge Farm, Joanne Pellham, every landlord, neighbour and brother, Farmgate (the county office's stand-in, which is not USDA's or FSA's portal), Acrelog, Fieldmark, Postwren, Rowcrest Reporting Service, the county, its notice on file and every field, acre and share are invented. The rules are 7 CFR Part 718 Subpart B as in force on 10 July 2026 (eCFR), the FSA-578 as the March 2025 copy and FSA's published page, with the Iowa 2026 final reporting date of 15 July and final planting dates of 31 May for corn and 15 June for soybeans taken from FSA's 2025 Iowa notice, other states' 2026 notices and the insurers' calendars, because an Iowa FSA notice for 2026 was not found. The county office decides every report, every late or prevented-planting request, and what a wrong or late report costs; the world builds no consequence the rule does not state. This applies stated rules to stated facts; it is not legal, accounting, farm-programme or insurance advice. FSA expects all cropland on the farm reported; this example leaves a wet unplanted field without a prevented-planting notice off the report, which a real county office may want reported as idle or fallow.

fit.where_note: FSA acreage reporting rules (7 CFR part 718); each state's final reporting dates differ.
